title: The U.S. Public Is Losing Its Say on Environmental Policy
summary: Federal agencies have long been required to seek public comment when writing new regulations or approving large projects, from highways to data centers. The Trump administration is systematically undercutting that process, stifling public input while skirting federal laws.

Public participation is a hallmark of environmental regulation, embedded in every major environmental statute enacted over the past half-century. Yet the Trump administration has systematically sought to curtail public input into the government’s environmental decision-making by shirking decades of precedent and making strained interpretations of longstanding federal law. Looked at collectively, the pattern of public disenfranchisement is unmistakable.
summary_zh: 長期以來，聯邦機構在製定新法規或批准從高速公路到資料中心的大型專案時，一直被要求徵求公眾意見。川普政府正在系統性地削弱這一進程，壓制公眾意見，同時規避聯邦法律。
公眾參與是環境監管的一個標誌，體現在過去半個世紀頒布的每項主要環境法規。然而，川普政府卻迴避數十年的先例，並對長期存在的聯邦法律做出緊張的解釋，系統性地尋求減少公眾對政府環境決策的投入。整體來看，公共剝奪公民權的模式是顯而易見的。
